newsitem.title: GERMANY: VULNERABLE GERMAN SHARES LOOK WEST FOR LEAD.
newsitem.headline: VULNERABLE GERMAN SHARES LOOK WEST FOR LEAD.

text.p: German shares were looking westward for direction on Tuesday afternoon, as thin volumes left the market vulnerable to shifts across the Atlantic and as key U.S. data loomed.
The IBIS DAX index was up 34.16 points at 4,367.31 points at 1355 GMT, just ahead of its closing bourse level, while September DTB DAX futures rose 59.5 points to 4,389.5.
Prices had earlier hit a high of 4,384.33 but faltered amid a shaky start on Wall Street.
"This is summer lull stuff," said a Munich trader. "People are a bit wary of some really crucial reports due in the U.S."
Data to be released in the U.S. on Wednesday includes retail sales and producer prices, both key indicators of inflation trends.
In Germany, the focus will be on chemical giant Hoechst AG, whose six-month results are due for release early in the session.
Chemical group Henkel KgaA HNKG-p.F was among Tuesday's top gainers after it reported a 10 percent advance in pre-tax profit to 438 million marks in the first half of 1997.
Henkel shares were up 3.80 marks, or 3.8 percent, at 104.40 marks in the afternoon.

Analysts expect Hoechst to post pre-tax profits of between 1.93 billion marks and 2.05 billion marks, down sharply from 4.32 billion marks in the year-ago period, when earnings were inflated by extraordinary income.
BASF AG is due to report its half year earnings on Thursday.

The broader market was benefiting partly on Tuesday from relief that the Bundesbank opted to leave its main money market rate, the repo, unchanged at 3.00 percent, confounding isolated expectations it would tighten its policy.
But some dealers still expected a rate hike in due course.
"It's a question of timing now," said one Frankfurt trader.
"It's naturally positive that the move did not come today but we were not looking for a change until the end of this month at the earliest."
